//: Copy to ~/.claude/keypad/config.json. Re-read once a second - no restart, no rebuild.
//label: slug = Claude Code's session name minus its random suffix (matches Warp's tab).
//label2: prompt = the opening prompt you typed.
label: prompt
//keys: The folder's bottom row, left to right. Each one also becomes a draggable action in
//keys2: Options+ under Claude Code in Warp > Commands, so you can put it on a home-page key.
//keys3: Remove this whole block to keep the built-in row: esc, /clear, /compact.
//keys4: An empty list gives all eight tiles to sessions. Seven keys is the maximum, so that
//keys5: at least one session tile always survives.
//text: text    typed into the pane, exactly as written (a trailing space is kept).
//submit: submit  press Return afterwards. Leave it off for commands you want to add to.
//key: key     "escape" interrupts instead of typing. Ignores text and submit.
//label3: label   what the key shows. Defaults to the text.
//ok: An empty text with submit is a bare Return - it answers a plan approval or a question
//ok2: dialog, which is the keystroke most worth saving if you run with plan mode on.
//safety: Anything here is typed into the focused Warp pane as if you had typed it, so treat
//safety2: it like a shell alias. It is passed to the system as an argument rather than
//safety3: interpolated into a script, so quotes and backslashes cannot break out.
